title: Channel Coding Converse via Fano's Inequality

problemStatement.formal: ∀ R > C, ∃ δ > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ code with rate ≥ R, P_e ≥ δ
problemStatement.plain: When transmission rate R exceeds channel capacity C, error probability is bounded away from zero for sufficiently long codes. Specifically, P_e ≥ (R-C)/(2R) for n ≥ 2/(R-C).
whyMatters: Proves the converse of Shannon's channel coding theorem — capacity is a sharp threshold
Provides a quantitative lower bound on error probability above capacity
Completes the formalization of the information-theoretic converse argument in Lean

proven: rate_ge_implies_log: R ≤ rate_of_code → nR ≤ log M
open: Strong converse: P_e → 1 as n → ∞ for fixed R > C
